problem: Large language models (LLMs) used in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) often produce unfaithful inline citations that do not accurately reflect the source of information, creating a misleading facade of credibility and an illusion of verifiability (p. 2-3).
methodology: The study uses mechanistic interpretability, specifically activation patching across residual streams, attention outputs, and MLP outputs between relevant and distractor runs, to reverse-engineer how Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct decides to emit inline citations (p. 2, 5, 6). The identified components are further evaluated and validated via targeted scaling interventions on failure cases, full PopQA distribution runs, and multi-document QA transfer on HotpotQA (p. 5-6, 8-9).
dataset: A citation-focused adaptation of PopQA using short single-fact questions paired with short supporting documents and structure-matched distractor documents, as well as a multi-document reasoning evaluation on 6,808 HotpotQA examples (p. 4, 9).
results: Amplifying identified pro-citation components with a scaling factor of alpha = 1.2 achieved over 90% citation recovery for missed citations, while down-scaling necessary components at alpha = 0.6 suppressed 69% of spurious citations in PopQA (p. 8-9). Applying the unified intervention to HotpotQA increased the strict correct citation rate more than 20-fold from 0.001 to 0.024 at alpha = 1.2 (p. 9).
key_findings: Inline citation decisions are governed by a distributed, multi-stage 'attributional ensemble' of attention heads and MLP layers that rely heavily on shallow heuristics such as entity co-reference matching rather than deep semantic integration during answer construction (p. 6, 7, 12). This ensemble acts via conjunctive AND-like dependencies that are asymmetric, making citation generation easy to disrupt but hard to induce (p. 7, 8).
limitations: The work analyzes only a single 8B model in a controlled setting, activation patching localizes components rather than directed information pathways, and the study did not directly map the answer-generation circuit to test mechanistic overlap with citation generation (p. 12). Additional limitations include the open question of generalizability to other datasets, models, and scenarios, and the potential risk of misuse in adversarial settings (p. 11-12).
title: How Do LLMs Cite?
